subsystems.name: Tissue preparation and scanning
subsystems.role: preserve a brain and image it at synaptic resolution.

subsystems.name: Connectome reconstruction
subsystems.role: turn raw images into a complete wiring diagram of neurons and synapses.

subsystems.name: Functional state mapping
subsystems.role: capture the electrical and chemical state of every neuron, not just its connections.

subsystems.name: Computational substrate
subsystems.role: run the emulation in real time or faster.

subsystems.name: Simulation software
subsystems.role: model neurons, synapses and their dynamics accurately enough to reproduce brain function.

subsystems.name: Embodiment and interface
subsystems.role: connect the emulation to sensors and actuators so it can interact with the world.

buildSteps.title: Preserve the brain
buildSteps.detail: Perfuse with fixatives to stabilise proteins and lipids, ideally after recording as much activity as possible from the living brain.

buildSteps.title: Slice and image
buildSteps.detail: Cut the brain into nanometre-thin sections and scan each with electron microscopy to reveal every synapse.

buildSteps.title: Trace the connectome
buildSteps.detail: Use machine learning to segment neurons and synapses from the images, then proofread the reconstruction manually or with AI.

buildSteps.title: Capture functional states
buildSteps.detail: Infer or record the electrical and chemical state of each neuron, using advanced imaging before fixation or computational inference from structure.

buildSteps.title: Build the computational model
buildSteps.detail: Convert the connectome and state data into a network of simulated neurons with realistic membrane properties and synaptic strengths.

buildSteps.title: Run the simulation
buildSteps.detail: Execute the model on a powerful computer, possibly using neuromorphic hardware, aiming for real-time operation.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and validate
buildSteps.detail: Compare the simulated activity patterns and behaviour against recordings from the original brain, adjusting parameters until they match.

buildSteps.title: Interface with the world
buildSteps.detail: Provide sensory inputs and read motor outputs so the emulation can interact with a virtual environment or a robotic body.

prerequisites.why: complete wiring diagrams exist only for small organisms like the nematode C. elegans; the human brain has about 86 billion neurons.
no current method can record the activity of every neuron in a living human brain at synaptic resolution.
exascale computers exist, but simulating a human brain in real time may require orders of magnitude more processing and memory.
we do not fully understand how patterns of neural activity represent information, which is needed to interpret and reproduce brain function.
techniques preserve small tissue samples well, but preserving an entire human brain with synaptic detail over the time needed to scan it is unproven.

pathway.milestone: complete connectomes of small organisms and partial maps of mammalian brains
pathway.unlocks: basic understanding of neural wiring and proof-of-concept simulations.

pathway.milestone: emulation of a simple nervous system, such as C. elegans, with behaviour
pathway.unlocks: demonstration that a whole organism's nervous system can be simulated.

pathway.milestone: emulation of a whole mouse brain
pathway.unlocks: mammalian-scale emulation and comparison with living behaviour.

pathway.milestone: emulation of a human cortical column or brain region
pathway.unlocks: partial human emulation and validation against human data.
digital immortality or space travel, if the necessary science and technology are ever achieved.
